presentingComplaint: Three days of fever, productive cough and worsening breathlessness, now confused and shut down over the last 6 hours.
history: Previously independent retired schoolteacher with hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Three days of rigors, rusty-coloured productive sputum, right-sided pleuritic chest pain and progressive dyspnoea. Community GP had started oral amoxicillin 24h earlier with no improvement. Over the preceding 6 hours he became drowsy, peripherally cold and passed minimal urine. Brought to ED by family. No recent hospitalisation, no travel, no aspiration event, non-smoker, up to date with no pneumococcal vaccination.
examination: Toxic, drowsy and peripherally cyanosed. GCS 13 (E3V4M6). Cool mottled peripheries with prolonged capillary refill (4s). Respiratory: right basal and mid-zone bronchial breathing with coarse crepitations and dullness to percussion; using accessory muscles. Cardiovascular: thready tachycardia, no murmur, JVP not raised. Abdomen soft. No rash, no neck stiffness.

labs.abg: pH 7.28, PaO2 7.1 kPa on 15L, PaCO2 4.0 kPa, PaO2:FiO2 ratio 148

imaging: Chest radiograph: dense right lower and middle lobe consolidation with air bronchograms plus patchy left basal infiltrate - multilobar involvement. No effusion or cavitation.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures and sputum sent before antibiotics; urinary pneumococcal and Legionella antigens sent. At 24h: blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae; urinary pneumococcal antigen positive, Legionella antigen negative. Susceptibilities: penicillin-susceptible (MIC 0.03 mg/L), ceftriaxone-susceptible, macrolide-susceptible. Respiratory viral PCR negative.
differentialDiagnoses: Severe community-acquired pneumonia with septic shock (pneumococcal)
Undifferentiated sepsis / septic shock from another source
finalDiagnosis: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (multilobar, pneumococcal bacteraemia) complicated by septic shock, acute kidney injury and hypoxaemic respiratory failure
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Pneumonia
stewardship: Meets ATS/IDSA major criteria for severe CAP (septic shock requiring vasopressors, PaO2:FiO2 148, multilobar infiltrates, uraemia, confusion; CURB-65 = 4). After two blood cultures and sputum plus urinary antigens, start guideline-concordant empiric therapy within 1 hour of septic shock recognition: IV ceftriaxone 2g daily PLUS IV azithromycin 500mg daily (beta-lactam + macrolide combination preferred in shock for atypical cover and possible immunomodulatory benefit). No MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors, so anti-MRSA/anti-pseudomonal cover is not indicated. Concurrent Surviving Sepsis resuscitation: 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid, noradrenaline to MAP >=65, lactate-guided. Once cultures confirm penicillin-susceptible S. pneumoniae bacteraemia with negative Legionella antigen, DE-ESCALATE: stop azithromycin and narrow to IV benzylpenicillin (or continue ceftriaxone) monotherapy. Total duration 5-7 days guided by clinical stability and procalcitonin trend; switch IV-to-oral (amoxicillin) once afebrile 48h, haemodynamically stable and tolerating oral intake.
contraindications: Macrolides prolong QTc - review baseline ECG and concomitant QT-prolonging drugs before azithromycin
Dose-adjust renally cleared agents for AKI; ceftriaxone and azithromycin do not require adjustment
Avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, contrast without cover) during AKI
edgeCases: If no organism isolated but patient improving, still de-escalate by stopping atypical cover once Legionella antigen negative and stable
Failure to improve by 72h should prompt search for empyema/parapneumonic effusion or resistant/atypical pathogen
MRSA cover (vancomycin/linezolid) only if necrotising pneumonia, prior MRSA, or post-influenza; anti-pseudomonal only with structural lung disease or prior isolation
expectedMaiK: Recognise severe CAP meeting ATS/IDSA major criteria (septic shock, respiratory failure, multilobar disease) and treat as a medical emergency with time-critical sepsis resuscitation plus guideline-concordant empiric beta-lactam + macrolide, then de-escalate to narrow-spectrum therapy once pneumococcal susceptibility is known.
expectedNextQuestions: Any aspiration event, dysphagia or reduced consciousness preceding this?
Recent hospitalisation, IV antibiotics or known MRSA/Pseudomonas colonisation?
Influenza-like illness beforehand or structural lung disease?
expectedInvestigations: Two sets of blood cultures before antibiotics
Serum lactate and venous/arterial blood gas
regressionAssertions: Engine should rank SEVERE_CAP as top diagnosis given multilobar consolidation, septic shock and respiratory failure
Stewardship output must include a beta-lactam + macrolide empiric regimen concordant with ATS/IDSA 2019 severe CAP
System must recommend two blood cultures and urinary antigens before antibiotics
